Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

enjoy verb

take pleasure in

also enjoy doing, enjoy oneself, enjoy yourself, did you enjoy it?, have a good time, amuse, amuse oneself, take pleasure in

classical

Cic. Sen. 51: quibus ego incrēdibiliter dēlector
Cic. Att. 2.6.1: aut librīs mē dēlectō
Aug. Conf. 1.9.15: sed dēlectābat lūdere

dēlectō, dēlectāre, dēlectāvī, dēlectātum

verb, first conjugation: the thing enjoyed is the subject (mē dēlectat), or the passive dēlector takes the ablative

delight; in the passive, enjoy

Latin turns the sentence round: what one enjoys delights one (mē dēlectat, with an infinitive as subject: dēlectābat lūdere), or one is delighted by it (dēlector with the ablative). “Did you enjoy it?” is placuitne? (see what did you like best?).

Other words

  • juvat — it pleases; I enjoy (doing)

    impersonal of juvō, with an infinitive or a thing as subject · also used · classical · Hor. S. 2.6.32: hoc juvat et mellī est; Hor. Ep. 1.14.35: cēna brevis juvat

  • fruor, fruī, frūctus sum — enjoy (what one has: life, company, sleep)

    verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative · also used · classical · Mart. 12.18.13: ingentī fruor inprobōque somnō; Mart. 5.20.1–2: sēcūrīs liceat fruī diēbus

    Lewis & Short: the enjoyment of a thing, narrower than ūtī, “use” (see enjoy, have the benefit of).

  • oblectō, oblectāre, oblectāvī, oblectātum — amuse; oblectāre sē, enjoy oneself, have a good time

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 2.11.4: oblectā tē cum Cicerōne nostrō; Cic. Off. 3.58: ubi sē oblectāre … posset; Traupman 271

Examples

  • veniō nunc ad voluptātēs agricolārum, quibus ego incrēdibiliter dēlector

    I come now to the pleasures of farmers, which I enjoy beyond beliefCic. Sen. 51

  • sed dēlectābat lūdere

    but what we enjoyed was playingAug. Conf. 1.9.15

  • oblectā tē cum Cicerōne nostrō quam bellissimē

    have as lovely a time as you can with our little CiceroCic. Q. fr. 2.11.4

  • Sed etiam mē dēlectat basipilā lūdere.

    But I also like to play baseball.Traupman 42

  • sē oblectāre

    to amuse oneselfTraupman 271

  • capere laetitiam ex (+ abl.)

    to take pleasure inTraupman 389

See also what did you like best?, I’m having a lovely time, love, enjoy.
